adversarialReview.challenge1: Am I calling a writer vacuous on a text search?
adversarialReview.response1: No. `grep -c 'kind: "value"'` across all 54 src/jobs files was used ONLY to pick which writers to READ; every vacuity claim in the artifact names a function and its branches read in full. Text search cannot answer a reachability question — that rule is why the grep is scored as a selector, not as evidence. Result: NO factory cell writer is vacuous. The vacuity is in the GATES and in one CI test.
adversarialReview.challenge2: Is `evaluateRailGate` returning ok:true on an all-unaccounted rail really a defect, or the intended declared-ahead semantics?
adversarialReview.response2: It is intended AND it is a defect, because the same return value encodes three different states: (a) nobody has built this writer, (b) the writer ran and wrote nothing, (c) the writer regressed and every cell reverted. The engine's own liveness.js header admits (a) vs (b) cannot be distinguished and names the run ledger as the backstop — but nothing joins the run ledger to the verdict. The `full-rail-poison` warning exists to separate (c) and its input `priorLiveRailKeys` is supplied by no caller (git grep: one hit, the read site). Starved, per ENFORCEMENT's own taxonomy.
adversarialReview.challenge3: Is the empty-county pass-through real, or would something upstream refuse first?
adversarialReview.response3: Traced end to end. evaluateOverlap returns EMPTY_DENOMINATOR on an empty want-set; evaluatePopulation branches only on code==='OK' or KEYSPACE_MISMATCH, so EMPTY_DENOMINATOR falls through all three gated comparisons. BAKE_POPULATION_MISSING requires roll.size > 0, so it does not fire either. loadCountyRailCells throws only on cells.length !== parcelRowCount, and 0 !== 0 is false. evaluateRailGate([]) -> cells.some() on empty is false -> ok:true, excluded. evaluatePreBakeReadiness clears on 'excluded'. Every link verified by reading the line, not inferred.
adversarialReview.challenge4: Two modules disagree about 46.9%. Did I pick a side?
adversarialReview.response4: No, and deliberately. publish-readiness-gate.mjs says parcel_record vs cad_property is the wrong comparison (accounts != parcels); county-rail-coverage.mjs makes exactly that comparison its denominator and calls the gap 'the never-instantiated share'. Both cannot be right about the same number. I report the disagreement with both citations and state the second mechanism for each, per ENFORCEMENT 'Reporting findings'. Adjudicating another module's closed finding is not this lane's call.

sectionBPivot: The mission's governing lesson (Harris: four checks agreed at 564,948 because all four read the same truncated input) has an exact structural analogue here and it is NOT hypothetical: the pre-bake RECORD_FILL_SHORT gate compares parcel_record against landing_parcel_jurisdiction, which is parcel-record-fill's own input population (LANDING_PAGE_SQL) and its own manifest denominator (fillCountyWide's `denominator: landing.n`, from LANDING_COUNT_SQL over the same table). Three of the pipeline's checks read one table. The one figure with an independent upstream (landing vs the CAD roll: Hays 69.34%, Travis 84.84%) is documented as REPORTED, NEVER GATED and attributed to accounts-per-parcel — an explanation that is consistent with a short layer ingest and does not distinguish it.
